sections.html:
Hall County's seat sits in central Nebraska a few miles north of the Platte River, roughly 1,870 feet above sea level. By the 2020 census only three Nebraska cities were bigger. Interstate 80 passes about 4 miles to the south, U.S. 30 cuts east to west through the middle, and U.S. 281 carries traffic north and south along the west edge. Central Nebraska Regional Airport is inside the city.

Buses on a fixed route do not exist here. Transit is entirely demand-responsive, with rides booked 24 hours ahead, so people drive. In your description, say how big the garage is, how wide the driveway runs, and how close Highway 281 or I-80 is.

Yearly precipitation averages about 26.6 inches and snowfall about 27.7 inches. May is the wettest month at 4.70 inches, and records range from minus 34 degrees to 117 degrees. Since May and June bring the heaviest rain, walk the grading around the foundation, the sump pump, window wells and crawl space yourself before a buyer's inspector gets there.

Tornadoes struck in 1980, and storm damage remains part of how locals talk about houses. Hail or wind repairs on yours? Hold on to the invoices, because they help you answer disclosure questions truthfully. Over 140 freight trains pass through daily, and a home close to the tracks may prompt questions.

The whole city lies in Grand Island Public Schools, whose comprehensive high school is Grand Island Senior High School. Private choices include Central Catholic High School and Heartland Lutheran High School.

Here is a wrinkle that catches buyers off guard. Northwest Public Schools operates a facility, Northwest High School among them, within the city limits, yet that district's taxing and attendance boundary takes in no part of the city. A parcel on the town's edge may belong to a different district, so read the district printed on the county tax statement and ignore the mailing address.

sections.h2: Selling a house with code problems
sections.html:
Under the city code, the Chief Building Official can direct an owner to make a dangerous building safe, with written notice sent by first-class and certified mail to the owner of record. A distinct Property Maintenance Code deals with litter, weeds, debris and other hazards on the premises.

  • Building Services covers the city plus a two-mile ring around it and enforces the 2021 International Residential Code with local amendments.
  • To schedule an inspection, call (308) 385-5325.
  • Landlords must supply, install, maintain and test smoke detectors.

Open code items do not block a sale, but the city can still write to the owner of record. Learn from the city what is outstanding before pricing, and tell the buyer in writing. Cash buyers price in the work. Lenders for financed buyers may refuse the loan until it is done.

Hall County is under 100,000 residents, so it runs on the standard schedule. A bill is due December 31, and delinquency begins May 1 for the first half and September 1 for the second.

DateWhat happens
January 1Real property is assessed
June 1The assessor mails notices of valuation changes
June 30Deadline for a protest and for a homestead exemption application
October 15Levy date
December 31Taxes are due
May 1 and September 1First and second halves become delinquent

Down the hall in Suite 2, the Hall County Treasurer publishes a delinquent tax list every year. Look for your parcel there before you list.

sections.h2: Deeds and the Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Deeds in Hall County are recorded at 200 South Sycamore Street, Suite 6, and the County Assessor is the contact for that office. A deed cannot be recorded without the Real Estate Transfer Statement, Form 521. The GIS viewer lists ownership and sale history for each parcel, so you can check your own record before a buyer does.

On the seller's side, the state's documentary stamp tax is $3.32 per $1,000 for deeds recorded from July 18, 2026.

Nebraska Revised Statute 76-2,120 asks you to describe appliances staying with the house, the electrical, heating, cooling, water and sewer systems, hazardous conditions, title matters like easements and encroachments, utility connections, and compliance with carbon monoxide alarm rules. A private transfer fee obligation goes on it too.

Mark an item unknown if you really do not know. The statute shields a seller from liability for errors outside personal knowledge, but concealing a known problem is not allowed. A buyer who never receives the statement may recover damages, costs and attorney's fees.

Get the parcel balance from the Treasurer and pass it to the title company, so the payoff comes out of your proceeds. A delinquent half will not stop the sale, though it belongs on the payoff list before anyone picks a closing date.

sections.h2: How a cash buyer changes the plan
sections.html:
Without a lender there is no bank appraisal and no loan committee. That counts for a Grand Island house with open code items, since a mortgage lender might decline to close until each is fixed.

Tax balances, the stamp tax and the disclosure statement are still yours to handle. Only the clock changes: it follows title work and how quickly the open items are sorted out.

A few errands pay off whichever way you sell. Ask the city for any outstanding items. Call the Treasurer for your tax balance. Open the county GIS viewer and see what a buyer sees about ownership and sales history. Collect hail and wind repair invoices. Then fill out the disclosure form, leaving an item as unknown only when that is true.

With those done, most of what a buyer or title agent asks already has an answer ready, and the closing is less likely to slip over a missing document or a forgotten balance.

sections.h2: Reading the tax calendar as a seller
sections.html:
The calendar above has a few dates that matter more to a seller than the rest. June 1 is when a valuation notice may arrive, and June 30 is both the protest deadline and the cutoff to apply for a homestead exemption. If you plan to list in summer, deal with the protest first, since a value you think is too high affects what a buyer expects to pay in taxes.

The levy date in October and the December due date matter at closing. The title company splits the current year's bill between you and the buyer, so ask for that split in writing and check that any delinquent half has been included in the payoff.

faqs.q: When are Hall County property taxes due and delinquent?
faqs.a: December 31 is the due date. In a county under 100,000 people, the first half goes delinquent May 1 and the second half September 1.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to protest a Hall County valuation?
faqs.a: June 30 for an individual real property protest. The assessor mails notices of valuation changes by June 1.

faqs.q: Is Grand Island's whole city in one school district?
faqs.a: Yes, Grand Island Public Schools covers it all. A Northwest Public Schools facility sits within the city limits, but that district's taxing boundary reaches none of the city.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Grand Island house that has code violations?
faqs.a: Yes. Open items do not bar a sale, though the city can still send notice to the owner of record. Find out what is outstanding and tell the buyer in writing.

faqs.q: Who pays the Nebraska deed tax when a house is sold in Grand Island?
faqs.a: You do, as grantor. The rate is $3.32 per $1,000 of value on deeds recorded from July 18, 2026, collected through the Hall County Register of Deeds.
